sentences.text: A prominent ridge running along the postorbital bone identifies this animal as a member of the gavialid family.
Unlike most modern crocodilians, some fossils suggest this creature was adapted to coastal marine habitats.
The genus name Eogavialis was proposed by Eric Buffetaut in 1982 to reassign species previously placed in Tomistoma.
The earliest specimens date back to the Priabonian stage of the late Eocene, between 37.2 and 33.9 million years ago.
Specimens from Kenya date to the late Miocene and early Pliocene, between 11.61 and 2.59 million years ago.
The fossil record spans from the Priabonian to the Messinian, covering 37.71 to 5.333 million years ago.
Eogavialis likely inhabited broad, shallow, meandering rivers in its environment.
Some researchers argue that several species previously named under Tomistoma are junior synonyms of Eogavialis africanum because they are morphologically indistinguishable.
